Senses.Explanation: The wave-off: a monk says even the master's beating is needless — and is beaten again; a congratulation is offered — needless; a ladle added at the bath — needless; even the master's own rope of talk — needless. The formula keeps its hands in its sleeves. The refusals in sequence: at Sanshan Denglai's hall the monk, beaten twice over, offers that even this beating is needless — the master beats him on and prices his own staff: deadly enough to kill a whole nest and den, let loose or gathered in, no mutual borrowing inside; Dahui Zonggao, when the mourning-talk runs to its cry of the gray heavens, rules that too uncalled for, and to the ask for his one sentence for people gives one rain moistening the whole sand-realm; Yezhu Fuhui, asked whether his teaching to a million humans and gods is the same or different, answers two throws, one contest — and when told, then it is celebration, answers: needless — before holding up the founder's mind-seal rising like a ridge, like a mound; Buhui Fatong at the birth-washing is asked to certify the vow as the student adds one ladle on the blind donkey's body — needless, he answers, and the exchange runs on to which pool has no moon; Shanhui Huan rules the holy and the common do not stay, and the hand-clap of before the empty kalpa has not yet one step — sparks and flint-light already fallen to second — then raises the whisk and dismisses even it: just this one, too, is needless; Qianshan Shengren Hanke closes his own turn: were someone with the eye at the crown of his head to step forward and say these two not only now never died but from the start were unborn, then this whole knotted rope of the mountain monk's talk is needless — flowers fall and flowers open, the spring colors yearly of themselves. The ancients waved off too: Guting Shanjian raises the old exchange — the one offers to strike only a chan-knowing fellow, and the answer comes back, needless — and rules the workman's hand and eye anything but common, the word-vein threading through, natural and at ease; Tianyin Yuanxiu raises the widow's case whole: of seven sons born, six met no soul that knew their worth — only this one, too, is needless — and she throws him into the water, and his verse sees the age on the clear stream looking only at the dear child, never at the widow.

Senses.Explanation: The responsive action displayed in an encounter: conduct that meets a changing occasion rather than merely following dead rules. Records say that Dahui exhausted or displayed all his responsive operation before Wuzu, that Wumen Huikai's and Yuelin Shiguan's responsive operation 'matched closely,' and that a portrait praise had Linji's responsive operation without indiscriminately carrying out staff-blows and shouts. Appraisals call it cutting, like thunder and lightning, or say it runs like thunder; instructional prose pairs living responsive operation with changing circumstances and contrasts it with dead rules. The compound also expands as 'great responsive operation' and joins recurrent predicates such as display, exhaust, match, be lively, run crosswise and lengthwise, or be fully raised. These are corpus descriptions of observable encounter conduct; the pivot or occasion graph (機) does not by itself name a student's graded capacity, and the records assign no single hidden purpose to the actions.

Senses.PreferredTarget: recorded Chan encounter
Senses.Explanation: A recorded Chan encounter is a public meeting or exchange preserved as a countable lineage case. The compound joins "occasion, trigger, or responsive capacity" (機) with "circumstance or connection" (緣). It appears as a section heading introducing successive exchanges, in the stable compound "question-and-answer encounters" (問答機緣), and in catalogues alongside entering-the-room encounters (入室機緣). One compilation calls the 1,700 old cases "1,700 encounters" (一千七百則機緣); the same author asks about "buddhas' and patriarchs' encounters, commonly called public cases" (佛祖機緣世稱公案者). The institutional deviation is therefore visible in record structure: an ordinary occasion or connection becomes a countable, titled public exchange preserved and revisited by the lineage.
Senses.Note: This technical sense does not turn every raw match into a formal interview. It preserves the texts' cautions: Zhongfeng Mingben lists seeking in encounters beside seeking in language and the 1,700 entangling vines, and Fangrong Tongxi raises the whisk while setting "encounter question-and-answer" aside. Family check: "question-and-answer" (問答) is the reciprocal verbal exchange; the individual-questioner turn formula has its own entry; "enter the room" (入室) identifies the room setting; "encounter" (機緣) is the wider encounter and its record. Fitting occasion or concord is separated below as a different referent. The headword has 1,568 occurrences in 303 allowlisted texts.

Yunhuan revoices it in a hall address after contrasting quick and slow responses; Yuanjie applies it in a sermon that moves from lofty formulation to ordinary sights and sounds. The mechanism is an image of responsive function, not a physical wheel. Retained public meaning is supported by independent present uses in recorded discourse.

Senses.Explanation: The sharp edge of an encounter is the quick, pointed capacity displayed when speakers meet in questioning and response. Records call it swift, steep, lightning-like, exchanged, or brought into contact with another's. The term can praise acuity, but criticism of merely rapid performance shows that speed alone does not establish success. It names the responsive edge being displayed or assessed, not a guaranteed result.

Senses.Explanation: Go north or south and ask old Wang: an image of seeking from another what direct seeing must resolve. Xuedou gives the original line; a later monk raises it to Yinyuan. Dahui, Tianru, and Chushi independently revoice it in letters, sermons, and verse to expose repeated doubt or outward search. Retained public meaning is supported by independent present uses in recorded discourse.

Senses.Note: The verse pictures questioners seeking Old Wang on both sides of a river, only to trade one doubt for another. Xuedou gives the pair in his verse on an old lotus exchange. Biefeng, Tianru, and Xuzhou voice it in distinct later sermons with their own questions and gestures. The repeated crossing changes no understanding by itself.

ClaimAnchors.Kwic: 身顯露，又作麼生？不怜鵝護雪，且喜䗶人氷。退鼓山云：長年追逐走埃塵，贏得閑名累此身。爭似別峯峯頂上，一菴高臥與雲隣。瑞巖受岳林辭眾云：巖谷相從始晏然，又携瓶錫應時緣。奉川此去無多遠，興發何妨訪戴船？古者道：人之所謂住，我則言其去；人之所謂去，我則言其住。去住雖殊，其致一也。恁麼說話，大似釘樁搖櫓，把󳮪放船。且不落去住一句作麼生道？青山藏不得，明月却相容。入院，云：衰老百無堪，擔頭入閙籃，生涯何所有？彌勒是同龕。當山祖師道：彌勒真彌勒，分身千百億，時時示時人，時人俱不識。師云：長汀子放憨作什麼？只今新長老來也，你須退後，還他出一頭地始得。大道只在目前，要且目前難睹。欲識大道真體，不離聲色言語。卓拄杖，云：者箇是聲。又竪起，云：者箇是色，喚什麼作大道？直饒向這裏見得，也是鄭州出曹門。尋牛須訪跡，學道訪無心。跡在牛還在，無心道易尋。竪起拂子云：者箇是跡，牛在什麼處？直饒見得頭角分明，爭柰鼻孔在岳林手裏。離四句，絕百非，頭長三尺知是誰。江北江南問王老，一狐疑了一狐疑。佛不遠人，即心而證。法無所著，觸境皆如。竪拄杖，云：若喚作拄杖，亦著於法。總不恁麼，瞎驢趁大隊。畢竟如何？遂靠拄杖，云：弄巧成拙。住法石，上堂。云：向上一路，千聖不傳。卓拄杖，云：恁麼明得，十萬八千。畢竟如何？桃紅李白薔薇紫，問著春風總不知。春已去，夏初臨。相逢休話本來心。隨緣齋粥海山寺，從聽堂前草自深。諸法寂滅相，不可以言宣。所以僧問風穴：語默涉離微，如何通不犯？穴云：長憶江南三月裏，鷓鴣啼處百花香。這箇是言宣，那箇是寂滅相？卓拄杖云：不用低頭，思量難得。施主看藏，云：演出演入，穿過髑髏；全藏半藏，換却眼睛。黃底非紙，黑底非墨，碧眼胡僧辨不得。以字不成，八字不是，百衲禪家不靈利。若靈利，撩起便行，高揖釋迦，不拜彌勒，奴呼菩薩，婢喚聲聞，其餘是甚盌躂丘？夫如是者，是真精進，是名真法供養如來，可以報生成之德，可以酬莫大之恩。然雖如是，且道某人生何國土？良久，云：不須他處覓，只此是西方。吾心似秋月，碧潭清皎潔。無物堪比倫，教我如何說？師云：大小寒山子，大似抱贓呌屈。若是山僧，又且不然。以拄杖打一圓相，云：騰騰離海嶠，漸漸出雲衢。諸人被十二時使，老僧使得十二時。牧童嶺上一聲笛，驚起群鵶繞樹飛。慶三門云：昔有一天使問睦州：三門俱開

Senses.Explanation: In the river country the spring wind cannot stir, and the partridge cries deep among the flowers. These are the opening lines of Xuedou Chongxian's verse on Fayan Wenyi answering ‘You are Huichao’ to the question ‘What is buddha?’ The Record Pointing at the Moon and Tianqi's notes transmit the full four-line verse under Xuedou's name, preserving this couplet as its opening rather than as free-standing landscape description. Feiyin Tongrong, Kuifu, and Dangui quote it while raising the Huichao case; Tieguan Shu speaks the couplet directly in a hall address before striking the whisk.
